title: Browser quest launch drops the MCP EmbeddedLaunchOverlay, so Wolf-Winter's delayed-dispatch opening is unreachable (finding #1, HIGH)
body:
Deferred from the 2026-08-28/29 audit fix pass. The finding was confirmed by an
adversarial verifier; it was not fixed in that pass for the reason below, which is
the fixing agent's own account after reading the code.

Cannot be fixed inside ui/** without duplicating engine trust logic. The derivation, `embeddedLaunchOverlayForPlan`, is a module-private function in src/mcp/overworld_quest_bridge.ts:68 (mcp subsystem) — it is not exported, and it re-verifies the dispatch window's schema version, quest id, ledger minutes and `proofHash` before minting the receipt. Reimplementing those ~40 lines in the UI is exactly what ui/README.md forbids ('Do not infer legality from prose, hard-code quest ids'). The clean fix is for the owner of src/mcp (or src/world) to promote it to shared engine code — e.g. src/world/quest_dispatch_window.ts — after which ui/src/engine.ts can thread an optional `launchOverlay` into `initStateForRpgPack`'s fourth parameter from both `startEmbedded` (engine.ts:194) and `restoreEmbedded` (engine.ts:226). Two owner decisions also sit on top of it: (a) what `overworld_session_id` the browser stamps into the receipt (the schema requires a non-empty string and there is no browser session id today; it must be deterministic because it is hashed into the quest state), and (b) that turning the overlay on invalidates in-flight browser Wolf-Winter saves whose recorded `stateHash` was computed without it — restore would fail closed on the recovery screen. The same promotion is what finding #1's sibling needs: `assertAuthenticatedQuestStartPreparation` (src/world/session.ts:483) is exported already and the UI could call it, but adding it alone changes nothing player-visible.
